Description:

This file takes two vectors of participant ids as input in order to specify two groups to compare. The file performs differential expression of transcriptomic data across the two groups. Given the ranked differentially expressed genes across the two groups, the file performs gene set enrichment analysis with the gseGO function from the clusterProfiler package. The file then visualizes the results to indicate the most differentially expressed gene sets across the groups.

## The following code blocks run GSEA with the gseGO function on the two specified groups of participants

### The following code loads the metadata files and processes them to produce a cleaned data frame of the combined metadata.

```{r}

# Takes in the metadata files for RNAseq and sample metadata
# This file is from https://ida.loni.usc.edu/pages/access/geneticData.jsp
RNAseq_metadata <- read.csv(file.path(main_directory, "PPMI_RNAseq_IR3_Analysis/metaDataIR3.csv"))
# This file is from https://ida.loni.usc.edu/web/ppmi-rnaseq-app#Accessdata
sample_metadata <- read.csv(file.path(main_directory, "meta_data.11192021.csv"))

# Checks dimensions and the number of unique samples in the metadata (should be the same)
dim(RNAseq_metadata)
length(unique(RNAseq_metadata$HudAlphaID))
dim(sample_metadata)
length(unique(sample_metadata$HudAlphaSampleName))

# joins the two metadata files and removes old files
RNAseq_metadata <- dplyr::rename(RNAseq_metadata, HudAlphaSampleName = "HudAlphaID")
joined_metadata <- inner_join(RNAseq_metadata, sample_metadata, by = "HudAlphaSampleName")
rm(RNAseq_metadata, sample_metadata)

# checks the dimensions of joined metadata compared to unique samples (should be the same)
dim(joined_metadata)
length(unique(joined_metadata$HudAlphaSampleName))

# stores the metadata filtered to only include samples that passed quality control
quality_metadata <- joined_metadata %>% dplyr::filter(QCflagIR3 == "pass")


dim(quality_metadata)

# joins genomic data to the RNAseq data in case downstream analyses consider the genomic data
genetic_metadata <- read.csv(file.path(main_directory, "iu_genetic_consensus_20250515_18Jul2025.csv"))
genetic_metadata <- genetic_metadata %>% dplyr::rename("PATNO.x" = PATNO)
overall_RNAseq_metadata <- left_join(quality_metadata, genetic_metadata, by = "PATNO.x")

dim(overall_RNAseq_metadata)
```


### This code block creates the gene expression count matrix for the two groups to compare

```{r}
# Gets just the relevant filtered sample IDs from baseline to use in setting up the counts matrix
filtered_sample_ids_bl <- sapply(sort(c(group_1_to_compare, group_2_to_compare)), function(patient_id) {(overall_RNAseq_metadata %>% dplyr::filter(PATNO.x == patient_id & Month == "M0"))$HudAlphaSampleName})

# Gets the label names for each gene from the first gene quanitification file
# Credit to https://stackoverflow.com/questions/42819131/read-tab-delimited-text-file
# for help with processing tab deliminations 
gene_names <- read.table(file.path(main_directory, "PPMI_RNAseq_IR3_Analysis/quant/PPMI-Phase1-IR3.1009.POOL.0003202425.5104-SL-0095.longRNA-NEBKAP.salmon.genes.sf"), sep = "\t", header=T)$Name

# creates data frame to store the expression matrix
tran_expression_counts_bl <- data.frame(gene_names)

# counter to help track progress of loop (see below)
counter = 0

# Fills the expression matrix with the data from each genomic file
# Credit to https://stackoverflow.com/questions/14958516/read-all-files-in-directory-and-apply-multiple-functions-to-each-data-frame
# for help with accessing all files in a directory
# Credit to https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/stringr/vignettes/regular-expressions.html
# for help with regular expressions
# Credit to https://www.dataquest.io/blog/add-column-to-dataframe-in-r/
# for help with manipulating data frames
# Credit to https://www.w3schools.com/r/r_for_loop.asp
# for help with setting up the for loop
gene_files <- list.files(path = file.path(main_directory, "PPMI_RNAseq_IR3_Analysis/quant"), pattern = "*.genes.sf")
for (x in gene_files){
    # determines if the file corresponds to filtered PD samples
    if(str_extract(x, "5104-SL-....") %in% filtered_sample_ids_bl){
      
        # adds the data from the file to the expression matrix.
        tran_expression_counts_bl[str_extract(x, "5104-SL-....")] <- read.table(file.path(main_directory, "PPMI_RNAseq_IR3_Analysis/quant/", x), sep = "\t", header=T)$NumReads
        
        # keeps track of counter and prints at every 100 counts
        counter <- counter + 1
        if (counter %% 100 == 0){
            print(counter)
        }
    }
}

# puts gene names as the row names
tran_expression_counts_bl <- column_to_rownames(tran_expression_counts_bl, "gene_names")

# sets the column names to be participant ids rather than sample ids
colnames(tran_expression_counts_bl) <- sapply(colnames(tran_expression_counts_bl), function(sample_id){(overall_RNAseq_metadata %>% dplyr::filter(HudAlphaSampleName == sample_id))$PATNO.x})

# orders the columns by ascending participant ids and rows by ascending Ensembl IDs
# Credit to https://stackoverflow.com/questions/29873293/dplyr-order-columns-alphabetically-in-r
# for help with this step
tran_expression_counts_bl <- tran_expression_counts_bl %>% dplyr::select(order(colnames(.))) %>% dplyr::arrange(row.names(.))
```



```{r}
# gets summary table with the numbers of participants by group in total and with transcriptomic data
data.frame(group = c("group 1", "group 2"), num_participants = c(length(group_1_to_compare), length(group_2_to_compare)), num_with_tran_data = c(sum(colnames(tran_expression_counts_bl) %in% group_1_to_compare), sum(colnames(tran_expression_counts_bl) %in% group_2_to_compare)))
```


### This code block creates a DESeq object with the metadata and expression counts.

```{r}

# sets up metadata file with cluster assignments of each patient
tran_DE_metadata_bl <- data.frame(participant_id = colnames(tran_expression_counts_bl))
tran_DE_metadata_bl$group <- as.factor(sapply(tran_DE_metadata_bl$participant_id, function(id){
                                              if(id %in% group_1_to_compare){return("1")}
                                              if(id %in% group_2_to_compare){return("2")}}))
tran_DE_metadata_bl <- column_to_rownames(tran_DE_metadata_bl, "participant_id")

# Checks that rownames in metadata match column names in counts matrix
# Credit to https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OzNzO8qwwp0
# for help with this step
all(colnames(tran_expression_counts_bl) == rownames(tran_DE_metadata_bl))


# Creates DESeq object with exp counts and metadata.
# Credit to https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OzNzO8qwwp0
# for help with this step
# Credit to https://support.bioconductor.org/p/133326/
# for help with debugging
GSEA_DES_obj_bl <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(countData = round(tran_expression_counts_bl),
                                          colData = tran_DE_metadata_bl,
                                          design = ~ group)
```

```{r}
# filters out genes that have all zero expression values
# credit to https://bioconductor.org/packages/devel/bioc/vignettes/DESeq2/inst/doc/DESeq2.html
# for help with this code
nonzero_rows_bl <- rowSums(counts(GSEA_DES_obj_bl)) > 0
GSEA_DES_obj_bl <- GSEA_DES_obj_bl[nonzero_rows_bl,]
```


### The following code blocks run differential expression analysis and compute the results

```{r}
# runs DESeq on the object and stores the results
# credit to https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OzNzO8qwwp0
# for help with these steps

# For the baseline data:
GSEA_DES_obj_bl <- DESeq(GSEA_DES_obj_bl)
DESeq_results_bl <- results(GSEA_DES_obj_bl)

```


```{r}
# Creates volcano plot of differential expression analysis results
# Credit to https://biostatsquid.com/volcano-plots-r-tutorial/
# for help with this step.
ggplot(DESeq_results_bl, aes(x = log2FoldChange, y = -log10(padj), col = (padj < 0.05 & !is.na(padj)))) + geom_point(size = 1)
```



```{r}
# gets a ranking of the most downregulated genes based on log2fc
downreg_ranked <- data.frame(gene_id = row.names(DESeq_results_bl) %>% substr(1,15),
                            log2fc = DESeq_results_bl$log2FoldChange) %>% arrange(log2fc)

# gets the downregulated genes and log2fc values in a named vector for gseGO
downreg_ranked_vector <- -downreg_ranked$log2fc
names(downreg_ranked_vector) <- downreg_ranked$gene_id

# reverses the vector to get the ranked list of most upregulated genes 
upreg_ranked_vector <- -rev(downreg_ranked_vector)

# checks the heads and lengths of the up- and down- regulated ranked vectors
length(upreg_ranked_vector)
head(upreg_ranked_vector)
length(downreg_ranked_vector)
head(downreg_ranked_vector)
```
### OPTIONAL code block that will filter the results to only a set of selected transcriptomic features 

```{r}
# loads the selected transcriptomic features from "PPMI_Data_Exploration_Transcriptomics_based_on_UPDRS.Rmd"
selected_tran_features <- read.table(file.path(main_directory, "selected_transcriptomic_features_from_UPDRS_A_vs_B.txt"))$V1
upreg_ranked_vector <- upreg_ranked_vector[names(upreg_ranked_vector) %in% (selected_tran_features %>% substr(1,15))]
length(upreg_ranked_vector)
head(upreg_ranked_vector)
```



### The following code blocks run the Gene Set analysis and display the results

```{r}

set.seed(648)

# runs the gsea analysis
# credit to https://www.rdocumentation.org/packages/clusterProfiler/versions/3.0.4/topics/gseGO
# for help with this code.
gsea_results_upreg <- gseGO(geneList = upreg_ranked_vector,
                            OrgDb = "org.Hs.eg.db",
                            keyType = 'ENSEMBL',
                            ont = "ALL")
```




```{r}
# creates dot plots of the gsea results
# credit to https://github.com/YuLab-SMU/DOSE/issues/20
# for help with this code
dotplot(gsea_results_upreg, x="NES", split = ".sign", font.size = 8, showCategory = 5) + facet_grid(~.sign) + ggtitle("All transcriptomic features - ALL terms")
```


```{r}
# converts results to a data frame
# credit to https://www.biostars.org/p/339493/
# for help with this code
as.data.frame(gsea_results_upreg)
```








## The following code blocks perform deconvolution analysis of cell types across groups 1 and 2


```{r}
# Gets just the relevant filtered sample IDs from baseline to use in setting up the counts matrix
filtered_sample_ids_bl <- sapply(sort(c(group_1_to_compare, group_2_to_compare)), function(patient_id) {(overall_RNAseq_metadata %>% dplyr::filter(PATNO.x == patient_id & Month == "M0"))$HudAlphaSampleName})

# Gets the label names for each gene from the first gene quanitification file
# Credit to https://stackoverflow.com/questions/42819131/read-tab-delimited-text-file
# for help with processing tab deliminations 
gene_names <- read.table(file.path(main_directory, "PPMI_RNAseq_IR3_Analysis/quant/PPMI-Phase1-IR3.1009.POOL.0003202425.5104-SL-0095.longRNA-NEBKAP.salmon.genes.sf"), sep = "\t", header=T)$Name

# creates data frame to store the TPM matrix
tran_TPM_bl <- data.frame(gene_names)

# counter to help track progress of loop (see below)
counter = 0

# Fills the expression matrix with the data from each genomic file
# Credit to https://stackoverflow.com/questions/14958516/read-all-files-in-directory-and-apply-multiple-functions-to-each-data-frame
# for help with accessing all files in a directory
# Credit to https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/stringr/vignettes/regular-expressions.html
# for help with regular expressions
# Credit to https://www.dataquest.io/blog/add-column-to-dataframe-in-r/
# for help with manipulating data frames
# Credit to https://www.w3schools.com/r/r_for_loop.asp
# for help with setting up the for loop
gene_files <- list.files(path = file.path(main_directory, "PPMI_RNAseq_IR3_Analysis/quant"), pattern = "*.genes.sf")
for (x in gene_files){
    # determines if the file corresponds to filtered PD samples
    if(str_extract(x, "5104-SL-....") %in% filtered_sample_ids_bl){
      
        # adds the data from the file to the expression matrix. USES TPM INSTEAD OF NUMREADS.
        tran_TPM_bl[str_extract(x, "5104-SL-....")] <- read.table(file.path(main_directory, "PPMI_RNAseq_IR3_Analysis/quant/", x), sep = "\t", header=T)$TPM
        
        # keeps track of counter and prints at every 100 counts
        counter <- counter + 1
        if (counter %% 100 == 0){
            print(counter)
        }
    }
}

# puts gene names as the row names
tran_TPM_bl <- column_to_rownames(tran_TPM_bl, "gene_names")

# sets the column names to be participant ids rather than sample ids
colnames(tran_TPM_bl) <- sapply(colnames(tran_TPM_bl), function(sample_id){(overall_RNAseq_metadata %>% dplyr::filter(HudAlphaSampleName == sample_id))$PATNO.x})

# orders the columns by ascending participant ids and rows by ascending Ensembl IDs
# Credit to https://stackoverflow.com/questions/29873293/dplyr-order-columns-alphabetically-in-r
# for help with this step
tran_TPM_bl <- tran_TPM_bl %>% dplyr::select(order(colnames(.))) %>% dplyr::arrange(row.names(.))
```





```{r}

# prints head of TPM matrix
head(tran_TPM_bl)

# adds gene symbols to matrix 
# credit to https://support.bioconductor.org/p/9138389/
# and https://support.bioconductor.org/p/130557/
# for help with this method
# credit to https://bioconductor.org/packages/stats/data-annotation/EnsDb.Hsapiens.v86
# for the EnsDb.Hsapiens.v86 package
tran_TPM_bl_with_symbol <- tran_TPM_bl
tran_TPM_bl_with_symbol$symbol <- mapIds(EnsDb.Hsapiens.v86, keys = substr(row.names(tran_TPM_bl), 1, 15), column = "SYMBOL", keytype = "GENEID", multiVals = "first")

# checks the number of symbols, NA symbols, and unique symbols
length(tran_TPM_bl_with_symbol$symbol)
length(!is.na(tran_TPM_bl_with_symbol$symbol))
length(unique(tran_TPM_bl_with_symbol$symbol))

# removes duplicated and NA symbols then checks that all symbols are unique
# credit to https://www.rdocumentation.org/packages/base/versions/3.6.2/topics/duplicated
# for help with the duplicated function
tran_TPM_bl_with_symbol <- tran_TPM_bl_with_symbol[!duplicated(tran_TPM_bl_with_symbol$symbol),] %>% dplyr::filter(!is.na(symbol))
length(tran_TPM_bl_with_symbol$symbol)
length(!is.na(tran_TPM_bl_with_symbol$symbol))
length(unique(tran_TPM_bl_with_symbol$symbol))

# sets the symbols to be the row names and examines the head of the data frame
rownames(tran_TPM_bl_with_symbol) <- NULL
tran_TPM_bl_with_symbol <- tran_TPM_bl_with_symbol %>% column_to_rownames("symbol")
head(tran_TPM_bl_with_symbol)
```

```{r}
# performs deconvolution analysis on the TPM transcriptomic data 
# uses the xcell method for the deconvolution analysis
# credit to https://omnideconv.org/immunedeconv/articles/immunedeconv.html
# and https://www.rdocumentation.org/packages/immunedeconv/versions/2.0.3/topics/deconvolute
# and https://github.com/dviraran/xCell
# for help with this method
deconv_results <- immunedeconv::deconvolute(as.matrix(tran_TPM_bl_with_symbol), "xcell") %>% column_to_rownames("cell_type")
deconv_results
```

```{r}
# performs wilcoxon tests on differences in each cell type across groups
# calculates the adjusted p-values and then sorts the results
wilcox_by_cell_type_results <- sapply(row.names(deconv_results), function(c_type){
  
    wilcox.test(unlist(deconv_results[c_type, group_1_to_compare]), unlist(deconv_results[c_type, group_2_to_compare]))$p.value
}) %>% p.adjust(method = "BH") %>% sort()

wilcox_by_cell_type_results


# acquires the wilcoxon effect sizes for differences in each cell type across groups
wilcox_effsize_by_cell_type_results <- sapply(names(wilcox_by_cell_type_results), function(c_type){
  
    wilcox_effsize(data.frame(deconv_exp = unlist(deconv_results[c_type,]), deconv_group = case_when(colnames(deconv_results) %in% group_1_to_compare ~ "Group 1", colnames(deconv_results) %in% group_2_to_compare ~ "Group 2")), deconv_exp ~ deconv_group)$effsize
})

wilcox_effsize_by_cell_type_results
```

```{r}
# creates boxplots to examine the direction of differences in each cell type across groups
sapply(names(wilcox_by_cell_type_results), function(c_type){boxplot(list("Group 1" = unlist(deconv_results[c_type, group_1_to_compare]), "Group 2" = unlist(deconv_results[c_type, group_2_to_compare])), main = c_type)})

# export a CSV of the significant results
# credit to https://www.rdocumentation.org/packages/VFP/versions/1.4/topics/Signif
# for help with the signif function
write.csv(data.frame(rank = c(1:length(wilcox_by_cell_type_results)), cell_type = names(wilcox_by_cell_type_results), BH_adj_pvalue = signif(unlist(wilcox_by_cell_type_results), digits = 2), wilcox_effect_size = signif(unlist(wilcox_effsize_by_cell_type_results), digits = 2), depleted_or_enriched = sapply(names(wilcox_by_cell_type_results), function(c_type){case_when(median(unlist(deconv_results[c_type, group_1_to_compare])) > median(unlist(deconv_results[c_type, group_2_to_compare])) ~ "Depleted", TRUE ~ "Enriched")})) %>% dplyr::filter(BH_adj_pvalue < 0.05), file.path(main_directory, "deconvolution analysis significant results.csv"))
```

### The following code explores GSEA according to beta values from the latent dimensions of iClusterBayes

```{r}

# for beta values from the 1st latent dimension of iClusterBayes

set.seed(648)

# runs the gsea analysis
# credit to https://www.rdocumentation.org/packages/clusterProfiler/versions/3.0.4/topics/gseGO
# for help with this code.
gsea_results_upreg <- gseGO(geneList = latent_dim_1_betas,
                            OrgDb = "org.Hs.eg.db",
                            keyType = 'ENSEMBL',
                            ont = "ALL")


# creates dot plots of the gsea results
# credit to https://github.com/YuLab-SMU/DOSE/issues/20
# for help with this code
dotplot(gsea_results_upreg, x="NES", split = ".sign", font.size = 8, showCategory = 10) + facet_grid(~.sign) + ggtitle("618 tran features - iClusterBayes Latent Dim 1 - ALL")
```

# creates dot plots of the gsea results
